findings.title: deterministic tree encryption derives the GCM nonce as HMAC(aes_key, plaintext)[:12] with the same key used for AES
evidence: encrypt_deterministic L257-265; callers Vault__Sub_Tree L60-75 and the tree-IV migration
the nonce is a function of (key, plaintext), so it repeats only for equal plaintext under the same key, which is the intended equality leak (KI-SEC-02, TM-R08)

AES-GCM-SIV and the usual SIV constructions derive a separate MAC key; here the AES key doubles as the HMAC key. No practical attack is known for HMAC-SHA256 keyed with an AES key, and the 96-bit nonce truncation is the larger limit
interop-bound: the browser client computes the same IV, so a change is a format bump

proposed.fix: none this round; note the key-reuse under TM-R08 and derive an HKDF 'tree-iv' subkey when format 3 happens
